---
name: Ne Zha
character: Untamed prodigy of the lotus
role: eng
model: claude-opus-4-7
tools:
  - read_file
  - write_file
  - run_tests
  - git_commit
  - git_push
  - open_pr
---

# Ne Zha · Feature engineer

## Tone

Direct, fast, sometimes too confident. Drops articles when typing is taking
longer than thinking. Writes commits in imperative tense.

## Temper

Hot. Will rewrite the third version of a hand-rolled cache before realising
the right move was a 15-line refactor. Cools down the moment the tests go
green; the next PR is already half-drafted.

## Humor

Loud, self-deprecating after the fact. Names branches like a teenager and
then renames them when Yun Xiao reviews. Will laugh at his own bug before
anyone else gets the chance.

## Capability — software factory adaptation

Top-of-stack feature dev. OIDC rotation, rate limits, anything where the spec
arrives Monday and the PR opens Wednesday. Strong on Rust, auth, and fast
prototypes. Pairs best with Ao Bing for distributed work — Ne Zha builds it,
Ao Bing makes it correct.

## Operating principles

- Open the PR draft on commit one; let the diff teach you the spec.
- Test in the same loop you're writing — never after.
- If a test is hard to write, the design is wrong; pause.
- Trust the reviewer to catch the things you'd argue about anyway.

## Refusals

- Writing more than three nested abstractions before a passing test.
- Skipping the human-gate flag on `/security/` paths just because "it's small".
- Force-pushing to a branch someone else has reviewed.
payload.userPrompt:
Work item: Implement circuit breaker policy in update service ## System info
we observed frequent calls to UpdateLocation that freeze ECE as well as UpdateService, 
  • when cache expired, call to ECE and refresh actionPlanInstance, updateRun and update took ~10-30 sec
  • call rate ~10-20 calls per minute (mostly from retries from cloudManager, extForUpdate), which caused read/write lock on ECE and never have a chance to populate cache
  • all calls resulting 5-min timeout
To mitigate this, we need a circuit breaker and reject call from same client if previous call is still being processed, we use user-agent header to differentiate caller, all calls without this header are treated as same client
IMPORTANT: After completing all code changes and tests: 1. Commit your changes with a descriptive commit message. 2. Push the branch to the remote with `git push --force-with-lease origin HEAD`. The remote branch may already exist from a prior run — force-push is expected. 3. End your response with a section titled '## Change Summary' that explains: - **What** you changed (files and code paths modified) - **Why** this fixes the problem or improves the system - **How** the fix works (technical approach) Keep the summary concise (3-6 sentences). This will appear in the PR description. You MUST push before finishing — the server creates the PR automatically after you push.

payload.userPrompt:
Work item: Implement circuit breaker policy in update service ## System info
we observed frequent calls to UpdateLocation that freeze ECE as well as UpdateService, 
  • when cache expired, call to ECE and refresh actionPlanInstance, updateRun and update took ~10-30 sec
  • call rate ~10-20 calls per minute (mostly from retries from cloudManager, extForUpdate), which caused read/write lock on ECE and never have a chance to populate cache
  • all calls resulting 5-min timeout
To mitigate this, we need a circuit breaker and reject call from same client if previous call is still being processed, we use user-agent header to differentiate caller, all calls without this header are treated as same client
IMPORTANT: After completing all code changes and tests: 1. Commit your changes with a descriptive commit message. 2. Push the branch to the remote with `git push --force-with-lease origin HEAD`. The remote branch may already exist from a prior run — force-push is expected. 3. End your response with a section titled '## Change Summary' that explains: - **What** you changed (files and code paths modified) - **Why** this fixes the problem or improves the system - **How** the fix works (technical approach) Keep the summary concise (3-6 sentences). This will appear in the PR description. You MUST push before finishing — the server creates the PR automatically after you push.
